{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"90bd30ec915da662c022229eb97c53bc95983194712126a7f054beebbf5b59ca","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Changing lanes, traffic, passing and enforcement","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Changing lanes, traffic, passing and enforcement","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Changing lanes, traffic, passing and enforcement

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A45
Before a lane change, check mirrors and blind spots, identify a gap, signal and look again toward the intended lane before adjusting speed and steering over. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A45
Blind spots are areas around a vehicle where obstructed views prevent mirrors showing pedestrians or vehicles. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A45
Vehicle design and roof pillars determine blind-spot locations, while dirty glass and glare may create temporary blind spots. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A45
Before turning or changing lanes, briefly turn the head to check for hidden road users. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A45
Avoid remaining in another driver’s blind spot, especially near commercial vehicles. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A45
On multilane roads, driving markedly faster or slower than surrounding traffic increases multi-vehicle crash risk. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A45
Driving faster than surrounding vehicles creates repeated passing situations, so slow to the traffic pace rather than repeatedly overtake. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A45
Driving much slower than other traffic can create queues and passing conflicts and may result in an impeding-traffic ticket. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A45
When vehicles queue behind, pull over only when safe to let them pass, then consider an appropriate pace or a road with lower posted speeds. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A45
Use an entrance acceleration lane to approach the speed of traffic before merging. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A45
Do not use up the acceleration lane and then stop, because that removes acceleration space and may surprise following drivers. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A45
If waiting for a merging gap is necessary, slow earlier on the ramp so room remains to accelerate before entry. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A45
Entering traffic must yield to vehicles already on the roadway. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A45
When an exit ramp is available, maintain traffic pace on the main road and reduce speed after entering the ramp. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A45
When turning off a fast two-lane road with traffic behind, avoid slowing unnecessarily early and use brief, safe brake taps before reducing speed. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A45
Recognizing slow vehicles early allows a lane change or gradual slowing instead of a sudden stop. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A45
Large trucks and small cars may lose speed on steep or long climbs and need more time to accelerate into traffic. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A45
Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and maintenance vehicles usually travel at 25 miles per hour or less and generally carry a rear slow-moving emblem. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A45
Slow when approaching those slow vehicles and pass to the left if possible, never to their right. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A45
Watch carefully for bicycles even though they should have reflectors or lights, because some lack them. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A46
Reduce speed in crowded areas to preserve reaction time when movement space is limited. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A46
Shopping areas, parking lots, downtown streets, rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges and tunnels are places where reduced speed may be needed. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A46
Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children who may enter without looking. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A46
Before a rail crossing, ensure no train is approaching and enough space exists to clear the crossing; slow for a rough crossing surface. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A46
On multilane roads, use the leftmost lane to pass slower vehicles and never pass on a shoulder, paved or unpaved. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A46
Complete a pass promptly and safely to minimize time alongside another vehicle. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A46
Before passing, check oncoming traffic, mirrors and over the shoulder for following or passing vehicles, then signal when safe. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A46
Steer smoothly into the passing lane and adjust speed as needed, continuing until the whole front of the passed vehicle is visible in the rearview mirror. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A46
Signal the return and steer smoothly back while maintaining or adjusting speed as necessary. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A46
When another vehicle passes you, stay in your lane and keep a constant speed. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A46
Do not attempt a pass with approaching oncoming traffic, a hill or curve blocking the view, at an intersection, or before a rail crossing or bridge. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A46
When passing a bicycle, slow down, leave as much room as possible and account for the bicycle’s speed. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

Misconceptions: A mirror does not reveal every blind spot; passing a bicycle uses the posted limit rather than the passing vehicle’s speed to choose the minimum separation; an enforcement stop does not justify stopping in the median.
Mnemonics: Use mirrors, shoulder, gap and signal as an authored lane-change cue.
Glossary: Blind spots are areas hidden from the driver’s view; an acceleration lane provides space to match entering speed; a vehicle projection includes an outside mirror.
Dynamic facts: Actual traffic speed, gap availability and stopping locations vary in real time; obey posted limits and actual officer directions.
